learning_outcomes.text: Students will be able to translate certain biological questions into a well-defined quantitative question that can be answered using basic concepts and models from physics.
Students will have learned how these models can be converted into systems of equations and how the solution (either analytical or approximate) is achieved.
Students will be able to interpret the obtained solution in light of the assumptions made when setting up the model and working out the solution.
Students will be able to relate this back to the original biological question.

syllabus_topics: Length and time scales in nature
Mechanical and chemical equilibrium in the living cell
Entropy in the living cell (including introduction to statistical mechanics)
Binary systems: from ion channels to cooperative binding
Beam theory: architecture for cells and skeletons

assessment_methods.method: Oral presentation of a biophysical topic (team assignment)

assessment_rules: The evaluation is based on a written exam (theory and exercises) and a homework assignment (oral presentation of a biophysics topic). The homework assignment counts for 10% of the total score if it has a positive effect on the overall score. The resit exam is the same as the first chance exam, and there is no resit for the homework assignment; its score can be carried over if it positively impacts the overall score.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
